evidence_causes.finding: These forms report an asset, income, or employment interest but do not report an acquisition/start date. A report date is not an ownership interval and cannot be substituted for one.

The extracted text layer is ambiguous, but every affected transaction row was reviewed on its rendered source page and visibly preserves a calendar-valid transaction date. This is a visual-recovery queue, not a structurally missing-date queue.
No temporally-unknown pair in this population was caused by a missing FEC aggregate earliest/latest bound.

home_depot_example.explanation: Five repeated HOME DEPOT INC investment rows each fan out to 128 FEC payee labels, many of which are store-number variants such as HOME DEPOT 0206 or HOME DEPOT #1519. Pair count is therefore not independent evidentiary support and corporate-family identity is not same-legal-entity identity.

visual_date_recovery.interpretation: All recovered transaction dates are in 2026, while every matched FEC aggregate latest date for these 45 pairs is earlier. Under the existing aggregate-range screen, all 45 move to non-overlapping and none opens identity review.

representative_source_page_reviews.visual_observation: Part 6 Other Assets and Income shows value and dividend-income columns, with no transaction or ownership-start date column.
The rendered transaction-date cell visibly includes the slash dropped by the extracted text layer.

representative_source_page_reviews.record: Northern Virginia Community College, spouse employment row 1
representative_source_page_reviews.visual_observation: Part 5 reports salary/employment but contains no employment start or end date.

adversarial_findings.finding: The current strictDate helper accepts impossible calendar dates such as 2025-02-30 because Date.parse normalizes them into March.
adversarial_findings.risk: An invalid date can be promoted as overlapping.

adversarial_findings.finding: The current screen treats an aggregate payee earliest/latest range as a continuous interval.
adversarial_findings.risk: A transaction date between two unrelated itemizations can appear temporally overlapping even when no FEC itemization occurred on that date.

adversarial_findings.finding: The machine-only date-recovery result of zero recovered dates is a text-layer result, not a source-page result.
adversarial_findings.risk: The rendered receipts visibly recover all 23 affected transaction rows, so describing the 45 associated pairs as unrecoverable discards observable evidence and leaves 45 resolvable pairs in the unknown bucket.

promotion_rule.annual_or_employment_records: Hold as structural/as-of evidence unless the form provides an explicit start/end/acquisition/disposition date. Never synthesize a full-year interval from report_date.
promotion_rule.ocr_transaction_records: Permit a date overlay only with a source-SHA/page/row-addressed visual correction receipt that records the visible token and a calendar-valid normalized date.
promotion_rule.fec_temporal_evidence: Require an actual itemization date and receipt; aggregate payee earliest/latest bounds may route research but may not establish event overlap.
promotion_rule.identity: Temporal coincidence only opens identity review. Promotion requires same-legal-entity resolution; corporate-family, brand, or store-label similarity is insufficient.
promotion_rule.final_status: Even after temporal and identity gates, preserve graph_effect none until holder scope, amendment/duplicate semantics, and both source receipts are resolved.
